anatomy.intro: Opposite pairs of fleshy paddles rise from a short central stem, with offsets forming at the base.

parts.function: The broad succulent leaf stores water.
parts.label: Fleshy paddle

parts.function: Leaves attach in pairs without a long leaf stalk.
parts.label: Opposite leaf pair

parts.function: The short central stem holds the upright leaves.
parts.label: Supporting stem

parts.function: A new side plant can continue growing after a flowering rosette declines.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: K. luciae has pale flowers with narrow lobes, while K. thyrsiflora has bright yellow flowers with broader lobes. These floral details help distinguish the two similar paddle plants.

growth.note: A flowering rosette completes its life cycle while its offsets can continue the clump.

stages.text: Young paddles enlarge around the central stem.
stages.title: Leaf rosette

stages.text: A mature rosette can send up a much taller flower stalk.
stages.title: Flowering rosette

stages.text: The flowering rosette dies, while surviving offsets can carry on.
stages.title: Offset renewal

habitat.text: The Kalanchoe luciae–thyrsiflora group comes from southern Africa. K. luciae occupies rocky slopes and hilltops in grassland and bushveld, including Eswatini. Upright paddles present their narrow edges to the midday sun, reducing the broad surface exposed to its strongest rays.

lookalikes.name: Kalanchoe thyrsiflora
lookalikes.text: Usually chalkier, with smaller leaves and yellow flowers; it is most easily separated from K. luciae when flowering.

mature.text: Flapjack rosettes commonly reach about 12–18 inches tall, with flower stalks several feet taller. Their broad leaves can shade smaller neighbors well before the flowering stage.

milestones.text: Acquired in the Smart Planet Home mixed succulent garden from Home Depot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

milestones.text: The rosettes, copper-toned shoots and broad paddles stayed together in the terra-cotta planter.
milestones.title: Repotted together

nameStory.text: The common name flapjacks refers to the stacked paddle leaves, like a loose pile of pancakes.
